sourceFindings: ReactiveElement saves pre-definition own properties before public addInitializer callbacks and orders replay by registered property metadata.
Unchanged atomState used throughout the fixtures; its TanStack atoms remain the owners of values and the declaration-order array.
Candidate omits CSS fields from Lit's normal property metadata, captures surviving own properties, and uses public observedAttributes/attributeChangedCallback handling.
Candidate uses no private Lit hooks; it requires a deliberate shared style metadata/attribute bridge and CEM declarations.
Ordered-object fixture preserves ordering and identity through ordinary Lit property registration; it is an evaluated alternative, not a selected public API replacement.

reactSource.finding: createComponent recognizes properties with k in elementClass.prototype, forwards element properties in incoming Object.entries order, and writes properties on every layout effect without value dirty-checking. Removed props become undefined.
reactSource.consequence: A keep-first-position capture alone cannot express reordered full React props. Plan an explicit per-render order synchronization in the house wrapper and verify it with React; do not equate setter update order with declaration order.

setupFailure.cause: The initial virtual Bun entry used standard-decorator emission instead of repository legacy-decorator settings, failing before the probe ran.
setupFailure.repair: Transpile virtual entry with TypeScript experimentalDecorators:true and useDefineForClassFields:false, matching repository settings, then bundle in memory.

limits: Chromium only; actual React, manifest analyzer, Firefox and WebKit integration were not run.
Candidate has only padding and paddingInline, not the full style API or production generated CSS.
Fixture retention/removal and mixed initial attribute/property behavior are candidate rules, not new user approvals of a complete cross-framework order protocol.

Subclass field/constructor defaults, registration/hydration variants, store-origin changes, external attribute reordering, direct React use, reactive reorder-only updates and generated metadata need deliberate checks.
No production files, project dependencies or generator outputs changed; builds served an in-memory fixture.
Only Lit's expected development-mode warning remained after the compiler setting repair; no console error in the successful run.
recommendation: Continue investigating a shared style-input module that preserves the selected separate properties using public APIs and the existing TanStack integration. Keep the ordered-object alternative as comparison evidence, not an approved API change.
next: Define and test the order protocol (including complete React prop sets and updates), prototype metadata/default handling, then return to the Box contract. Do not claim the gap fully closed from this two-property probe.
